instructions:
gotchea quiz display rules:
- Show everything between <<<SHOW TO USER VERBATIM and SHOW TO USER VERBATIM>>> verbatim: the code block with its path:line header, the question and all four options in full.
- Show every block between <<<SHOW ANSWER FEEDBACK TO USER VERBATIM and SHOW ANSWER FEEDBACK TO USER VERBATIM>>> verbatim: the correct option, the explanation and the cited code.
- Never replace option text with short labels. If you offer a selection UI, label its choices only A, B, C, D.
- Ask the question to the user, do not guess the answer yourself.

tools.name: get_chunk_for_file
tools.description: Find the chunk covering a file position. With `line`: the innermost chunk containing it. Without: the file chunk followed by its leaf chunks. Served from an in-memory index.

path.description: File path relative to the repo root

line.description: 1-based line; the innermost chunk containing it is returned

tools.name: get_generation_tasks
tools.description: The next chunks that need quiz questions, highest priority first (no questions yet, most imported, largest gap). Each task has chunk-relative numbered code, import signatures, the stems of existing questions and the instructions. Write the questions yourself, then call save_questions. Best done in a subagent or a separate session, so the answers you write stay out of the context you are quizzed in.

lang.description: Question language code such as en, tr or pt-BR; defaults to config questions.lang

tools.name: get_map
tools.description: The comprehension heat map: repo > module > file > symbol, with colour (⬜ unseen, 🟥, 🟨, 🟩), LOC and question counts. Optionally filtered by path and limited in depth.

path.description: Only this directory, file or chunk id, relative to the repo root

depth.description: Levels below the (filtered) root to include; unlimited when omitted

tools.name: get_status
tools.description: Tracked chunk count, question count, reviews due now and the colour distribution of the leaf chunks.

tools.name: save_questions
tools.description: Save questions you wrote for one task from get_generation_tasks. Pass the task chunkId and chunkHash unchanged. If the chunk is unknown or its code changed (hash mismatch), the whole call is refused and nothing is saved. Otherwise each question is validated and saved, and rejected ones come back as { index, reason, detail }. Fix those and resubmit only them.

chunkHash.description: chunkHash of the generation task; a mismatch means the code changed and the whole call is refused

lang.description: Question language code such as en, tr or pt-BR; defaults to config questions.lang

questions.description: Raw questions: { type, stem, options: [4 strings], correctIndex: 0-3, explanation (cites L<n>), refs: [{start, end}], difficulty: 1-3 }. Line numbers are chunk-relative, as in the task code.

tools.name: scan
tools.description: Chunk the repository and update the map: detects added, changed, moved and removed chunks. Runs synchronously and may take a while on large repos.

tools.name: start_quiz
tools.description: Start a comprehension quiz on one chunk of this repository. Pass `path` (a directory, file or symbol: the chunk that most needs review under it is picked) or `chunkId`; with neither, the whole repo is considered. Optional `count` shortens the quiz (default: the chunk's size, 3–7). Returns the first multiple-choice question with the code it is about, between verbatim relay markers. Show the user everything between the markers verbatim, exactly as written: the code block with its header, the question and all four options in full. Do not shorten, paraphrase or drop any of it. Ask the question to the user, do not guess the answer yourself. If you also offer a multiple-choice selection UI, label its choices only "A", "B", "C", "D" (the full text is already in your message). After an answer, also show the answer-feedback block between its own markers verbatim: the correct option, the explanation and the cited code. Then call `submit_answer` with the option the user picked. The correct answer and explanation are revealed only after you submit.

path.description: Directory, file or chunk-id prefix, relative to the repo root

count.description: Questions in this quiz; clamped to [quiz.minQuestions, the chunk size]

lang.description: Question language code such as en, tr or pt-BR; defaults to config questions.lang

includeCode.description: Attach the chunk's source to each question (default: the config value quiz.showCode, true unless set; a resumed session keeps its own). The preview is the working-tree source, so the quiz is open book.

tools.name: submit_answer
tools.description: Submit the user's answer to the current quiz question. `displayIndex` is the position of the option the user picked, as shown by `start_quiz` or the previous `submit_answer` (A=0, B=1, C=2, D=3). Answers are final and must be given in order. Returns an answer-feedback block (whether it was correct, the correct option, the explanation and the cited code), then the next question with its code, each between verbatim relay markers. Show the answer-feedback block verbatim too. Show the user everything between the markers verbatim, exactly as written: the code block with its header, the question and all four options in full. Do not shorten, paraphrase or drop any of it. Ask the question to the user, do not guess the answer yourself. If you also offer a multiple-choice selection UI, label its choices only "A", "B", "C", "D" (the full text is already in your message). After an answer, also show the answer-feedback block between its own markers verbatim: the correct option, the explanation and the cited code. After the last question this returns the result: pass/fail, the chunk's new colour and an updated mini heatmap.

questionId.description: questionId of the question being answered

displayIndex.description: Position of the option the user picked, as displayed: A=0, B=1, C=2, D=3

includeCode.description: Attach the chunk's source to the next question (default: the session's value, set by start_quiz from includeCode or quiz.showCode, default true). The preview is the working-tree source, so the quiz is open book.
